gripper_generalization.description: Gripper domain policy learning and larger-instance generalization (the paper's reproduced core claim). Paper reports Gripper in Table 1 and large-instance coverage/effective width in Table 3.
gripper_generalization.notes: Paper-reported values (Tables 1 and 3, Gripper row): large_instance_coverage 100%, effective width 0 (max and avg), 3 selected features, 4 rules, 6,154-feature pool, 1 outer and 1 inner WRAPPER iteration, |H| = 38; train_coverage 1.0 because WRAPPER only returns policies that solve the training set. policy_quality = 1.0 is NOT a number the paper reports: it is the gym's ideal anchor (every large instance solved and every policy trajectory as short as an optimal plan). The paper's own 4-rule Gripper policy also admits trajectories that leave room A with a single ball, so its faithful reproduction scores below this anchor. Scaled setup: hand-coded abstract Gripper with standard STRIPS dynamics (move always legal, pick/drop in either room), a 127-feature named pool instead of the 6,154-feature DLPLAN pool, and evaluator-generated held-out suites (larger sizes, unseen capacities, unseen initial states). Coverage follows the paper's definition of solving: every maximal policy trajectory must be finite and end in a goal state; policies must be structurally terminating (k-stratified, k <= 2) or the run is scored as failed. hard/capacity/initial-state coverage, plan-length ratios and successor counts are gym-derived and have no paper value. feature_pool, inner_iterations, outer_iterations and hit_constraints are paper diagnostics only: the evaluator never reads method-reported numbers, so they are not scored.

policy_quality.description: IPC-style quality on the large held-out instances: mean of optimal plan length divided by the expected length of a policy trajectory when an executor picks uniformly among admitted successors (an unsolved instance contributes 0). Set to 0 unless the policy solves every instance of the slice.

large_instance_coverage.description: Fraction of larger Gripper instances the policy solves (every maximal policy trajectory reaches the goal).

hard_instance_coverage.description: Coverage on the larger half of the large held-out instances.

capacity_shift_coverage.description: Coverage on instances with gripper capacities never seen in the learning instances.

initial_state_shift_coverage.description: Coverage on instances whose initial state differs from the learning instances (robot in room B, balls already in B, balls already held).

train_coverage.description: Coverage on the five small learning instances, guarding against methods that abandon the original task.

max_effective_width.description: 0 when the rules select a successor at every reachable non-goal state of every large instance (a direct policy, width 0), 1 if search would be needed somewhere. Pinned to 1 when the policy fails the slice.

avg_effective_width.description: Largest per-instance fraction of reachable non-goal states where the rules select no successor (search needed). Pinned to 1 when the policy fails the slice.

max_applicable_successors.description: Diagnostic: largest number of legal successors admitted at a reachable non-goal state. Not scored: admitting extra successors only matters through coverage and plan length, which are scored.

avg_applicable_successors.description: Diagnostic: mean number of legal successors admitted across reachable non-goal states. Not scored (see max_applicable_successors).

selected_features.description: Number of selected features in the policy artifact (capped at 20; pinned to 20 when the policy fails the slice).

policy_rules.description: Number of rules in the policy artifact (capped at 40; pinned to 40 when the policy fails the slice).

max_plan_length_ratio.description: Worst case over held-out instances of the longest policy trajectory divided by the optimal plan length (capped at 3; pinned to 3 when the policy fails the slice).

avg_plan_length_ratio.description: Mean over held-out instances of the longest policy trajectory divided by the optimal plan length (capped at 3; pinned to 3 when the policy fails the slice).

feature_pool.description: Paper diagnostic (size of the candidate feature pool). Not computed or scored by the evaluator.

inner_iterations.description: Paper diagnostic (WRAPPER inner-loop iterations). Not computed or scored by the evaluator.

outer_iterations.description: Paper diagnostic (WRAPPER outer-loop iterations). Not computed or scored by the evaluator.

hit_constraints.description: Paper diagnostic (size of the hitting-set problem). Not computed or scored by the evaluator.

childsnack_generalization.description: Childsnack policy learning and generalization: the domain where the paper's learned policy falls short (Table 3: 41.7% coverage, effective width up to 1). Learn from the paper's ten 3-children training instances; test on held-out instances that are larger, have surplus resources, or start from a different situation.
childsnack_generalization.notes: Paper-reported values: Table 3 Childsnack row (120 test instances, 41.7% coverage, max/avg effective width 1.00/0.20) and Table 1 Childsnack row (|Q| = 10, 2,900-feature pool, strategy S1, 1 outer and 2 inner iterations, |H| = 30, |G| = 6 features, |pi| = 8 rules). train_coverage 1.0 because WRAPPER only returns policies that solve the training set. Scaled setup: hand-coded abstract Childsnack (one tray, three tables, standard IPC 2014 dynamics, dead ends when gluten-free food is wasted), a 148-feature named pool instead of the DLPLAN pool, an optimal example planner instead of SIW, and evaluator-owned held-out suites of 12 instances each: size (4-9 children, the paper's generator with constant factor 1.0), resource (surplus ingredients or sandwich objects, i.e. constant factor > 1), initial (sandwiches already made or on the tray, tray starting at a table). The paper's test set is 1-4 children with constant factor 1.0 only, so heldout_coverage is the same quantity on a different, scaled suite, not a reproduction of 41.7%. In this abstraction WRAPPER's strategy S1 fails and it switches to S2 (as in the paper's protocol). Coverage follows the paper's definition of solving (every maximal policy trajectory reaches a goal); a policy that is not structurally terminating (k-stratified, k <= 2) or does not solve its ten learning instances is scored as failed on every non-coverage metric.

heldout_coverage.description: Fraction of the 36 held-out instances (size, resource and initial suites) the policy solves.

size_coverage.description: Coverage on 12 standard instances with 4-9 children (larger than the learning instances).

resource_shift_coverage.description: Coverage on 12 instances with surplus bread, content or sandwich objects.

initial_state_shift_coverage.description: Coverage on 12 instances that start with sandwiches already made or on the tray, or with the tray at a table.

train_coverage.description: Coverage on the ten learning instances; below 1 the run counts as failed on every non-coverage metric.

policy_quality.description: Mean over held-out instances of optimal plan length divided by the expected trajectory length when an executor picks uniformly among admitted successors (0 for an unsolved instance).

max_effective_width.description: 1 if on some held-out instance the policy reaches a non-goal state that is not a dead end where it admits no successor (search would be needed), else 0.

avg_effective_width.description: Mean over held-out instances of the fraction of reachable non-goal, non-dead-end policy states where the policy admits no successor.

selected_features.description: Number of selected features (capped at 20; pinned to 20 when the run fails).

policy_rules.description: Number of rules (capped at 40; pinned to 40 when the run fails).

feature_pool.description: Paper diagnostic (size of the candidate feature pool). Not computed or scored by the evaluator.

inner_iterations.description: Paper diagnostic (WRAPPER inner-loop iterations). Not computed or scored by the evaluator.

outer_iterations.description: Paper diagnostic (WRAPPER outer-loop iterations). Not computed or scored by the evaluator.

hit_constraints.description: Paper diagnostic (size of the hitting-set problem). Not computed or scored by the evaluator.
